reader.requirement: At --std 85 an OPEN naming several file-names (in one or several mode groups, of any organizations) behaves as one OPEN per file-name in source order: each file gets its own mode and status, each unsuccessful one runs its USE procedure before the next file is opened, and a later file-name sees the effect of an earlier one (a file created by an earlier OUTPUT, a file opened by an earlier occurrence of the same name).
reader.edition-search: SequentialIoBinder.BindOpen (one BoundOpen per file-name in a BoundImplicitSeries, source order) and SequentialIoEmitter.EmitOpen (a per-file loop) read: no EditionContext, DialectLevel, CobolVersion or DialectBehavior reference in either; the only edition gate on the statement is VersionConformancePass's refusal of the 2002 SHARING phrase, which is not this rule.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for the decomposition; the outcome of a later file-name on the same physical file differs because the 2002 sharing facility (Table 19) is off at 85
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_f19_03 covers two mode groups and the failure order on two absent files; same-physical-file ordering, one file-name written twice, and mixed organizations in one statement are not exercised

reader.notes: The binder decomposes the statement into one BoundOpen per file-name and the emitter writes, per file, BeginOpen, the open, the FILE STATUS store and the USE hook, so the per-file order and the USE-before-next-file order follow from the code shape at every edition.

refuter.evidence: Probe runs/r17_useopen-001: OPEN INPUT QD OUTPUT QC, where QD is absent and QD's USE procedure itself OPENs QC OUTPUT. It printed USE QD 35 QC 99 / USE OPENED QC 00 / USE QC 41 / AFTER OPEN QD 35 QC 41 / WRITE QC 00. That is exactly the separate-statement order: QD's status and USE run before QC is opened, and QC's later open sees the earlier effect (41).
